# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Emerson Hayes**
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
By phone: 1-888-333-4742 (Member Services)

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 4, 2026**
- **Member:** Emerson Hayes
- **Member ID:** W807153430
- **Reference number:** POC-9668BA39E4-60948
- **Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
- **Governing policy:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316), available at https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the knee arthroscopy (CPT 29881) that my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented is needed. The notice states that the request was denied because the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to reconsider that decision, because the records in the prior authorization packet document a long and complete course of conservative treatment, and because the findings in my chart line up with the plan's own published criteria.

## What the plan's policy says, and what my records show

**1. The plan's own tip sheet directs reviewers to the full guideline.**

The plan's policy states:

> "The guidelines should be reviewed for additional requirements including duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria and for the complete listing of other procedures not included below."

I want to be straightforward with you about one point. The excerpts of the Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet that I have been able to obtain set out conservative-care requirements for lateral release and for debridement chondroplasty. **I have not been given, and therefore am not quoting, any specific conservative-care criterion for meniscus surgery.** The argument below on that point is in my own words, and it compares my records to the durations and treatment types the plan itself publishes elsewhere in the same document. If the plan is applying a specific written criterion for CPT 29881, I respectfully ask that the exact language be identified in the appeal response so I can respond to it directly.

On the items this quoted sentence names — duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria — my records contain all three:

- **Duration of symptoms:** 12 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical examination:** positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Radiographic criteria:** MRI of the knee dated May 24, 2026, showing a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking; articular cartilage preserved; Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1.

**2. The conservative-care periods the plan publishes are 6 months and 12 weeks. My records exceed both.**

The policy states:

> "(Evolent Guideline 316) 5— Knee Arthroscopy Clinical Tip Sheet ❖ Lateral Release • Failure of at least 6 months of non-operative treatment, including quadriceps strengthening and appropriate hamstring/IT band stretching and patellar mobilization techniques, and at least one of the following:"

and:

> "oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection ❖ Debridement chondroplasty for patellofemoral chondrosis • Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following:"

and lists as qualifying non-operative treatment:

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment:"

My records document the following, all before surgery was requested:

| The plan's listed treatment | What my records show |
|---|---|
| Physical therapy modalities / quadriceps strengthening | Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion — 14 weeks, March 30, 2026 to July 6, 2026, 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDs | NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief |
| Corticosteroid injection | Injection on April 23, 2026, giving 2 weeks of partial relief |
| Rest or activity modifications/limitations | 12 months of pain unrelieved by rest; I am limited to level walking and cannot squat or kneel |

That is **more than two** of the treatment types the plan itself lists, a 14-week supervised physical therapy course that exceeds the 12-week period the policy uses, and a 6-month medication trial that matches the 6-month period the policy uses. The treatment also failed: my symptoms are progressive, the injection relief lasted two weeks, and I continue to have locking and giving way.

**3. My imaging is consistent with what the policy says about grading.**

The policy states:

> "MRI should not be the primary tool used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

and sets out the grading scale:

> "Grade Description 0 No radiographic features of osteoarthritis 1 Possible joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation 2 Definite osteophyte formation with possible joint space narrowing 3 Moderate multiple osteophytes, definite narrowing of joint space, some sclerosis and possible deformity of bone contour 4 Large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of bone contour"

My records state a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 1 and preserved articular cartilage. My MRI is not being used to grade arthritis; it identifies a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. That is a mechanical problem, and mechanical locking is not something more physical therapy or another injection is likely to resolve.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to overturn the denial dated August 4, 2026 (reference POC-9668BA39E4-60948) and approve CPT 29881 as requested by Dr. Marchetti. I also ask that:

1. The review be conducted by a physician with orthopedic surgery expertise.
2. The specific written criterion applied to CPT 29881 be identified in the response, with the exact policy language quoted.
3. The following records be considered in full: the physical therapy discharge note covering March 30 to July 6, 2026 (24 visits); the medication and injection records, including the corticosteroid injection of April 23, 2026; the MRI report of May 24, 2026; and Dr. Marchetti's office notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **January 31, 2027**. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and Member Services can be reached at 1-888-333-4742.

Thank you for taking another look at this. I have done everything that was asked of me before surgery, over the course of a year, and I would appreciate a decision that reflects what is in the record.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Hayes**
Member ID: W807153430
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
Signature: ______________________
Date: ______________________

**Enclosures:** [List of records enclosed — e.g., physical therapy discharge note; medication/injection records; MRI report dated 2026-05-24; office notes from Dr. Marchetti; copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-04]
